# Experience handoff

Reuse existing product artifacts where possible. Give small changes a short
handoff; new core journeys may need the full sequence. The coordinator connects
the evidence, interface contracts and exit criteria.

| Stage | Artifact content |
| --- | --- |
| Research/framing | Buyer/task evidence, sourced friction, experience goal and unknowns |
| Flows/IA/states | Entry/action/result, navigation and ownership; loading, empty, error, retry, cancellation |
| Wireframe/prototype | Realistic content, hierarchy, critical journey and failure paths |
| Visual/component system | Adopted direction, tokens, typography, components, responsive rules and copy |
| Working vertical slice | Implemented behavior, interface contracts, data states and owned files |
| Usability/accessibility/rendered QA | Task result, keyboard/focus, mobile/desktop, screenshots/traces and linked defects |

For each applicable stage, record:

- Inputs and governing contract/decision IDs.
- Artifact path and revision captured by the ledger.
- Decisions, assumptions, alternatives, risks and scope exclusions.
- Responsible owner, criteria IDs and next action.
- Actual observation, source and evidence gap; agent review is distinct from
  customer research, and automated accessibility checks are not full conformance.
